Owner decision, 17 Nov 2026: 'Ok let's lower the bar.' Thrum is a game engine; the aim is the most plausible result as fast as possible, not physical accuracy. New bar for rendering and visual work: it looks as good as shipped high-end games, judged against an agent-written visual inspection list, and it runs fast, with performance as tripwires (no invented budgets). Physical or f64 references stop being pass/fail gates: they stay as diagnostic tools used when output looks wrong, to find the cause. Exact image baselines stay only where they guard against unintended regressions, not to block deliberate shader changes. Correctness proofs stay where failures are silent and costly: networking and transport, simulation determinism, asset and cooked formats, contracts between modules. Also make proof proportional to risk: small fix rounds and tripwire records shouldn't get the same review weight as new rendering work, and cut evidence items that cost more than the risk they cover.
